trust_boundaries: external-to-dmz: external_saas webhooks and end_user OAuth to dmz components
dmz-to-internal: webhook_receiver/oauth_proxy to event_queue and rate_limiter
internal: event_queue to transformer to integration_db and audit_log
architecture_summary.operational_context: SaaS integration hub receiving events from external providers and routing to internal systems

threat_actors.name: Malicious SaaS Event Source
threat_actors.motivation: Inject malicious payloads via webhooks to compromise integration pipeline
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Forged or replay webhook events to webhook_receiver endpoint
non_capabilities: No direct access to event_queue or internal components
No OAuth tokens for end_user flows
No access to audit_log for covering tracks
No ability to modify transformer logic directly

threat_actors.name: Compromised End User
threat_actors.motivation: Data access beyond authorised scope via OAuth token misuse
threat_actors.initial_access_vector: Stolen OAuth token from client-side exposure or phishing
non_capabilities: No access to webhook_receiver admin configuration
No ability to modify audit_log entries

attack_paths.entry_point: Unauthenticated or weakly authenticated webhook endpoint
attack_paths.impact: Event injection into integration pipeline; SSRF or payload injection into transformer
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Webhook HMAC signature verification is often missing or disabled; publicly documented attack pattern

attack_paths.entry_point: Stolen OAuth 2.0 access token from end_user session
attack_paths.impact: Authorised API calls beyond user's intended scope if token scopes are overly broad
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: OAuth token theft via client-side exposure is common; overly broad scopes amplify impact

attack_paths.entry_point: Template injection or expression evaluation in payload transformation logic
attack_paths.impact: Code execution within transformer service, access to integration_db
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Template injection in data transformation is common (Jinja2, OGNL); requires specific transformer implementation

attack_paths.entry_point: Rate limiter bypass via distributed source IPs or header manipulation
attack_paths.impact: Flood of malicious events overwhelming transformer and integration_db
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Rate limiter bypass techniques are well-known; distributed attack tools are commodity

attack_paths.entry_point: Authorised queries via transformer exposing schema structure
attack_paths.impact: Database schema enumeration revealing sensitive data structures for targeted follow-on attack
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Requires AP-003 or AP-002 first; schema exposure is lower severity but enables more precise attacks

attack_paths.entry_point: Bulk data read via compromised transformer (AP-003)
attack_paths.impact: Mass exfiltration of integration data including third-party access tokens stored in DB
attack_paths.likelihood_rationale: Requires AP-003 success; exfil of stored OAuth tokens would be highest-impact outcome

mitigations.control_name: Webhook HMAC signature verification with replay prevention
OAuth scope minimisation and token rotation
Input sanitisation and safe template rendering
Distributed rate limiting with source IP reputation scoring
Database access control — query row limits and read-only service accounts

findings.severity_rationale: Missing webhook signature verification allows any party to inject events; high external attack surface exposure
Template injection in transformer provides code execution; stored OAuth tokens in integration_db are high-value exfiltration target
OAuth scope creep enables access beyond intent; mitigated partially by planned minimisation
Stored tokens in integration_db are exfiltration-ready if DB access is obtained; no encryption at field level
Rate limiter bypass is mitigated by IP reputation; residual distributed attack risk remains but impact is availability, not data
